findings.F1: Over the next day, a coin's excess return over its normal drift rises steadily as its latest day's return, in units of its 60-day daily standard deviation, falls. It is +1.19 % (t 3.54, 334 cases) after falls beyond 2 standard deviations, +0.37 % (t 2.42, 1154) after falls of 1 to 2, +0.16 % (t 1.72, 2842) after falls of 0.3 to 1, −0.13 % (t −1.82, 4156) after flat days and −0.18 % (t −2.27, 2921) after rises of 0.3 to 1. These t's are not day-clustered.
findings.F2: The rebound shows on the first day and fades with the horizon. After falls beyond 2 standard deviations, the excess is +1.19 % over 1 day (t 3.54) but +0.77 % over 2 days (t 1.74, 185 cases) and −1.26 % over 5 days (t −1.21, 57 cases). The tested 2-day horizon therefore holds a rebound that is mostly over after one day.
findings.F3: The tested grading by turbulence shows in the 2-day excess after falls beyond 1 standard deviation. It is +1.63 % (t 3.71, 308 cases) when the 10-day to 60-day volatility ratio is in its top quarter, against −0.91 % (t −1.30, 62 cases) in its bottom quarter. In forecast terms, it is +0.57 % (t 3.32, 1929 cases) at forecasts above 15, against −0.41 % (t −2.12, 1046) at forecasts of 0 to 5. The gain sits almost entirely at the capped top of the forecast.
findings.F4: The book is mostly the coins' own market move, not the rebound. Its daily return correlates 0.785 with the coins' mean daily return. On its worst 2 % of days it lost 8.2 % while the coins fell 10.7 %. It trails holding in every rising year (for example 2021: +0.18 % against +0.41 % a day) and beats it only in 2018 and 2022. Being in a position on 83 % of days is what carries the falls that fail the Calmar test (0.68).
findings.F5: After a strong rise there is a hint of continuation, not reversal: +0.87 % 2-day excess after 5-day returns above 1.5 standard deviations (t 2.36, 475 cases), +3.4 % 5-day excess after up days beyond 2 standard deviations (t 2.14, 89 cases), and +0.81 % 2-day excess after 5-day up streaks (t 1.85, 208). These overlapping cases, with unclustered t's near 2, come from roughly 90 cells examined, so this does not yet stand out from chance.
findings.F6: The weekday pattern does not stand out once coins sharing a day are counted together. Mean 1-day excess is +0.30 % on Fridays (t 3.76) and −0.30 % on Wednesdays (t −2.70), but these t's are unclustered over six coins that move together. The pattern also has no grading.

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's fall on its latest day, measured against the size of its own daily moves over the past 60 days, the more it rises over the next 1 day.
ideas.consequence: A trader takes a one-day rebound after an unusually large daily drop, sized by how unusual the drop is, and is out the next day instead of carrying the market's falls for two days.
ideas.name: one-day rebound after unusual fall

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's fall on its latest day against its 60-day daily moves, the more it rises over the next 1 day, and the more so the larger its daily moves over the past 10 days are against those of the past 60 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader keeps the turbulence grading of the tested idea but shortens the rebound bet to the one day in which it shows.
ideas.name: turbulent fall one-day rebound
